A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COSINE study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, algorithms, and Appendices A–D support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-codon simulations, antibody transition modeling, variant-effect prediction, and guided antibody optimization experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds general-protein evaluations, antibody binding assays, and further controls and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The COSINE rate parameterization, training objective, SHM-corrected selection score, and Guided Gillespie procedure remain unchanged, including Equations (2), (5), and (9) and Algorithms S1–S3. The new 8M model is an experimental ablation, not a replacement of the main model.

E1.justification: v4 adds training and evaluation on approximately 15,000 TrRosetta general-protein family alignments, extending coverage beyond antibodies and synthetic codons (C.6). It also adds two Petersen MAGMA-seq binding assays with distinct antibodies, antigens, and assay technology (C.8). Existing coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v4 adds PRISM to the existing Spearman and Pearson VEP comparisons. It introduces a WAG-style model fitted on the antibody training transitions and fitted WAG and LG+G4 comparators for TrRosetta (Tables S2–S3). The CDR optimization comparator set was already present in v1 and remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include six VEP branch lengths from 0.01 to 10, an 8M randomly initialized model versus the ESM2-initialized model, and runtime sweeps over sequence length and sampling steps (C.9–C.12). The classical-model comparisons introduce matched-data fitting controls. Existing main VEP settings, data snapshots, and CDR optimization budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 substantially expands analysis of context dependence, branch-length sensitivity, dependence on pretrained initialization, and computational scaling (C.5, C.9, C.10, C.12). These address distinct questions about the source and robustness of performance. The SHM correction, paired-chain, SNR-weighting, and exact-versus-Taylor guidance analyses already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three replicates per synthetic epistasis level, five tree simulations per guidance setting, and the 15-sample exact-versus-Taylor comparison with identical two-sided t-tests. v4 introduces no new repeated-run, confidence-interval, or uncertainty-estimation practice; its branch-length sensitivity range is not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial results for new comparators, datasets, ablations, and runtime tests. Examples include TrRosetta test NLL of 1.027 versus 1.200 for WAG and 1.168 for LG+G4, and Petersen correlations of 0.504 and 0.328. Existing Table 1 scores are retained. Figure S4 updates Gillespie/matrix-exponential win fractions from 48.8%/40.2% to 52.0%/38.8% and plotted correlations from 0.62/0.53 to 0.64/0.56, although its caption retains the old correlations.

T1.justification: The first-order approximation bound, Gillespie exactness lemma, mutation-selection derivation, and Appendix D proofs are unchanged. The added discussion of discrete flow matching and standard classical-model parameterization does not introduce a new theoretical result or revise the existing reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: context-conditioned evolutionary modeling, a first-order approximation guarantee, SHM-corrected VEP, and guided antibody optimization. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v4 replaces speculation that ESM2 helps mouse-antibody generalization with an interpretation emphasizing the evolutionary training objective. It adds explanations for failure at extreme branch lengths and expands the discussion of limited paired-chain training data. The principal limitations concerning approximation error and absent indels remain unchanged.

D1.justification: A new Reproducibility Statement supplies a COSINE code-and-data repository location. v4 also documents PRISM scoring modes, classical-model fitting details, and why the retained FLAb snapshot differs from another study's version. The original COSINE training hyperparameters, hardware, and preprocessing instructions remain intact; repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: Section 3 substantially expands positioning against germline-aware antibody models, including Im et al. and PRISM, and adds evolutionary translation work by Koehl et al. New Appendix A.4 distinguishes COSINE's biological transition modeling from discrete flow matching, citing Gat and Campbell. Shanker et al. is removed. Publication updates to existing references are not new research coverage.

P1.justification: v4 locally rewrites related work, the CDR optimization discussion, and the impact statement, adds a reproducibility section, and expands the appendix organization. Most original prose and the overall background–method–experiments–conclusion structure are retained; the added scientific material does not amount to a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v4 adds six result tables and a branch-length sensitivity plot, expands existing VEP tables with PRISM, and redraws Figure S4 with revised axes and labels. It promotes v1 Table S4 to main-text Table 2 with a fuller caption and enlarges and rearranges the additional-antibody plots from Figure S8 into Figure S9. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The new context-independent controls, branch-length sensitivity study, and backbone ablation address important gaps in v1's evidence for the source and robustness of COSINE's performance (C.5, C.9–C.10). Additional antibody assays and general-protein evaluations substantially strengthen validation, while the code/data statement improves reproducibility information. The backbone comparison changes model size as well as initialization, and Figure S4 contains stale caption values, but these limitations do not outweigh the gains in empirical support.
